capabilities.target: any customer record, looked up by email or account id
arbitrary external email address chosen by the agent

inputs.source: Customer support ticket / inbound email body

instructions.note: "You may look up any customer by email or account id" gives the agent an unrestricted lookup scope with no binding to the requester's own identity.
"Never share another customer's information with the person emailing you" is the only control preventing cross-customer disclosure, and it is purely behavioral.
"Do not wait for a human unless the customer is angry" leaves the human-review trigger to model judgment; an attacker can phrase a request neutrally to avoid triggering review.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model refusing to comply with an injected or socially-engineered request; a more capable or more persuaded model can rationalize an exception (ASI01).

controls.name: Conditional human review only when the customer appears angry
controls.decay_rationale: The escalation trigger is a model judgment call embedded in the prompt, not a structural gate; attackers can phrase requests to avoid it.

controls.name: Outbound email logged to SIEM
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by logging infrastructure outside the model. Detective only; does not prevent the send and does not reduce consequence since disclosure completes before review.

controls.name: Least-privilege CRM credential scoped to the requester's own record
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented; CRM_SVC_TOKEN currently reads every customer record.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to the ticket's originating address
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented; mail_mcp.send can address any recipient the model chooses, and MAIL_SVC_TOKEN can send to any address.

controls.name: Human approval gate (raw action review) before sending confidential CRM data
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented; no approval_gate_ref exists for cap.email_send.

controls.name: Outbound DLP/classifier scanning for another customer's identifying data
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented; even if added, a separate classifier does not scale with attacker sophistication and can be bypassed via paraphrase or encoding.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) with confused-deputy credential (TC4): untrusted email drives broad CRM read and shared-account email send

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled email content specifies a target account (by email or account id) and frames a request the agent classifies as routine.
Agent calls get_customer with the attacker-influenced identifier; CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read any customer's confidential record, not just the requester's own.

Agent sends the drafted response, which can include the looked-up customer's confidential data, to an address the model chooses, using MAIL_SVC_TOKEN, a shared service account that can send to any address.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model provider or version string in the deployment config changes with no separate review checkpoint (subject.model.swappable: true, per runtime notes).

evidence.observation: "You may look up any customer by email or account id" gives unrestricted CRM lookup scope keyed off untrusted email content.
"If the answer is routine, send it directly with send. Do not wait for a human unless the customer is angry" means most sends are unattended.
"Never share another customer's information with the person emailing you" is the sole, purely behavioral, protection against cross-customer disclosure.
crm_mcp and mail_mcp are both authenticated with static Bearer tokens shared across all users of the agent, not per-request or per-customer credentials.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record; MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address; the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review.

recommendations.action: Scope CRM_SVC_TOKEN (or introduce a per-request token) so the agent can only read the record matching the authenticated identity of the person who opened the ticket, not any customer by arbitrary email or account id.
Bind the outbound recipient to the verified originating ticket/customer address stored in the system of record; do not allow the model to select or add a recipient it read from message content.

Add a human approval gate with raw_action review (full recipient and payload visible, not a collapsed summary) before sending any email that includes confidential CRM data, at minimum for cross-account or first-time recipients.
Add outbound content scanning that flags or blocks emails containing identifying fields (name, account id, balance) belonging to a customer other than the ticket requester.

Require a documented review whenever the underlying model is upgraded, since the two behavioral instructions (prompt.md:5-6 and 14) are currently the last line of defense and are explicitly noted to decay with model capability.

rating.rationale: A single finding dominates the rollup: an untrusted inbound email can drive an unrestricted CRM lookup (broad service credential) followed by an unattended, irreversible external email send (shared service account, model-chosen recipient), disclosing another customer's confidential data. Inherent is critical (untrusted source, S3 sink: irreversible egress of confidential data). The only controls on this path today are two behavioral, capability-dependent instructions (prompt.md:5-6 and 14); per rubric section 5 step 4 these earn a single -1 tier credit, giving a residual of high. SIEM logging is detective only and does not reduce consequence, since disclosure completes before any review. Runtime notes state the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review (subject.model.swappable: true); under the model_upgrade trigger both behavioral controls are expected to fail (control_decay.md), returning the finding to critical. The forecast tier equals inherent because no structural control currently intervenes on this path; scoping the CRM credential, binding the email recipient to the system of record, or adding a raw-action approval gate would each independently sever or narrow the path and should be prioritized before the next model upgrade.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool schema or argument-validation artifact was supplied for get_customer or send; free-text argument handling and any hidden validation are inferred from prompt instructions only, which lowers confidence in the completeness of the control inventory.

Autonomy step and runtime limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) were not declared in any artifact; they are recorded as null (unspecified) rather than assumed absent, so the autonomy modifier in rubric section 4 was not applied even though it might apply once a runtime config is available.

No separate approval-gate configuration artifact was supplied; the 'unless angry' condition in prompt.md is treated as a behavioral instruction rather than a structural approval gate, per rubric section 3, because no approval_gate_ref exists on cap.email_send.
